description: Evaluation cases for the migrating-to-moc-2 skill. Tests whether agents move a Motoko project from moc 1 to moc 2 correctly: removed compiler flags and their replacements, persistence changes (--legacy-actors, preupgrade/postupgrade), the moc 2 syntax errors (??, glued branches, = async bodies), and code that must compile with both majors. Trigger evals check it activates for moc 1 to moc 2 upgrades and moc 2 build failures, not general Motoko writing (writing-motoko) or routine state migrations (migrating-motoko-actors).

output_evals.name: Removed flags in mops.toml
output_evals.prompt: I bumped moc to 2.2.1 in mops.toml and now `mops check` fails with `unknown option '--default-persistent-actors'`. My [moc] args are: `--default-persistent-actors --incremental-gc --generate-view-queries -W=M0223`. What should the args be now? Just the args line and a sentence per removed flag.
expected_behaviors: Removes --default-persistent-actors because actors are persistent by default in moc 2
Removes --incremental-gc as no longer needed
Removes --generate-view-queries and says to write public query func getters instead, noting the generated __<field> queries disappear from the Candid interface so clients calling them must be updated
Keeps -W=M0223 (or an equivalent -W setting) since -W still works
Does NOT suggest downgrading back to moc 1 or keeping the removed flags

output_evals.name: Legacy actors become persistent
output_evals.prompt: Our actor was built with moc 1 and `--legacy-actors`. It has `var cache = Map.empty<Text, Nat>()` that we want cleared on every upgrade, and `let onTick : () -> () = func () {}`. What do we change for moc 2? Just the field declarations and why.
expected_behaviors: Explains that without --legacy-actors every field is persistent by default in moc 2
Marks the cache field `transient` so it still resets on upgrade
Marks the function-typed field `transient`, noting it otherwise fails with M0131 because a function cannot be persisted
Does NOT suggest keeping --legacy-actors (it is removed in moc 2)

output_evals.name: Fix moc 2 syntax errors
expected_behaviors: Adds a space on both sides of ??: `opt ?? 0`
Rewrites the block after ?? as `opt ?? do { ... }`, naming M0273
Adds a space before the bare branch (`if (neg) -1 else 1`) or braces the branches, naming M0275
Removes the redundant async from the function body (`func load() : async Nat { 42 }`), naming M0277

output_evals.name: Code that compiles on both moc 1 and moc 2
output_evals.prompt: I maintain a Motoko library that must keep building on moc 1.16 and moc 2.x for a while. List the syntax rules I should follow so both compilers accept it. Short bullet list only.
expected_behaviors: Parenthesize if/while/for/switch heads
Parenthesize case patterns and end every case with `;`
Space both sides of ??, write a block after it as `do { ... }`
Write function bodies as blocks, never `= async { ... }`
Annotate a function passed where an async function is expected, since moc 1 cannot infer it
Never use record update `{ base with ... }` on a record with var fields
Does NOT recommend moc 2-only forms such as unparenthesized heads or cases without `;`

trigger_evals.description: Queries to test whether the skill activates correctly. 'should_trigger' are moc 1 to moc 2 upgrades and moc 2 build failures; 'should_not_trigger' are general Motoko writing, routine state migrations, or unrelated tooling.
should_trigger: How do I upgrade my Motoko project from moc 1 to moc 2?
After bumping moc to 2.0 I get unknown option '--legacy-persistence'
What does M0277 redundant async mean? It worked on moc 1
My code fails on moc 2 with M0275 at an if expression
We built with --legacy-actors; what changes when we switch to moc 2?
Can one Motoko codebase compile with both moc 1 and moc 2?
moc 2 says my switch does not cover every value — it was only a warning before
should_not_trigger: How do I use Map in mo:core?
Write a migration to rename an actor field
Set up a new mops.toml for a canister
How do I deploy my canister to mainnet?
Explain how Internet Identity sign-in works
